note: Stage 4 rebuild empty-weight inputs (AER-3784, MANUFACTURING, 2026-10-24; revised to the stage 3 revision 2 shortlist). Signed deltas in lb: light = lightest credible outcome, heavy = heaviest. Grades as in the long list: F factory, T TCDS, P pilot report or flight test, B builder or registry data, R measured record, E our estimate. The engine swap is not among the items; engine_delta_lb is [most saving, least saving] from our per-variant engine check (docs/MANUFACTURING.md#engine-check), on AERO's Aeromomentum rule (dry x 1.25 + 35 lb). Laminate arithmetic behind the composite items is in docs/MANUFACTURING.md#how-the-composite-deltas-are-built.

base.basis: 1,550 published spec (F, Prescott via 1000aircraftphotos.com, read 2026-10-24); no as-built weighing found. Heavy end +100 lb for an equipped kit build (E). The 1986 design target was 1,220 lb (P, AOPA Pilot Mar 1986): the airframe grew 330 lb before the published spec

items.item: Fuselage shell: non-structural composite shell over the 4130 cage, re-made in infused carbon (cage kept)
items.basis: Shell is non-structural (P, AOPA Pilot 1986), so only the laminate changes: about 200 ft2 (E; no wetted area yet) at 2 plies, glass 0.11-0.12 against carbon 0.066 lb/ft2 per ply

items.item: Wing: flush-riveted aluminium, built-up spars and ribs (110.8 ft2) -> molded carbon wing
items.basis: Metal GA wing about 2.0-2.5 lb/ft2 of exposed planform (Raymer, approximate weight build-up), about 190-240 lb; a molded carbon wing saves 10-25% (E)

items.item: T-tail: aluminium -> carbon
items.basis: Tail areas not published; about 40-60 lb of tail (E)

items.item: Panel: 1980s avionics -> EFIS

items.item: Replace the 4130 cage too: structural carbon monocoque fuselage
items.basis: Cage about 90-140 lb for a four-seat tube fuselage (E); a load-carrying shell adds most of it back; loses the cage's crash protection; needs STRUCTURES
